svg.text: PAYMENT GATEWAY — CHARGE & REFUND FLOW
THE TRANSACTION STATE MACHINE
PENDING
created, not yet charged
charge() == false
charge() == true
FAILED
terminal
SUCCESS
captured, refundable
partial refund → stays SUCCESS
remainingRefundable() == ZERO
REFUNDED
terminal — accepts nothing further
applyRefund throws
from FailedTransactionState
no money moved ⇒ nothing
is refundable
legality lives in the state object, not in scattered if-checks ✓
THE AUTH / CAPTURE FOLLOW-UP — the machine absorbs it
Insert AUTHORIZED between PENDING and SUCCESS, plus an AuthorizedTransactionState
allowing capture() → SUCCESS and void() → CANCELLED, but NOT applyRefund.
No service changes at all — that is what the State pattern bought ✓
THE REFUND CRITICAL SECTION
① RESOLVE — txn = getTransaction(transactionId)
missing ⇒ TransactionFailedException, never a silent null
the registry hands back the CANONICAL instance — which is what makes the next step work
② synchronized (txn) — ONE section, four things
synchronized (txn) {
if (amount == null || !amount.isPositive()
|| amount.compareTo(txn.remainingRefundable()) > 0)
throw new IllegalArgumentException(...); // (a) BOUND
TransactionStateFactory.forStatus(txn.getStatus())
.applyRefund(txn, amount); // (b) LEGALITY + (c) LEDGER
Refund r = new Refund("REF-" + n, txnId, amount);
refundsFor(txnId).add(r); return r; } // (d) AUDIT ROW
(a) bound (b) legality (c) running total + status flip (d) audit row — all inside ✓
Splitting ANY of them out reopens the race.
The bound check and the legality check are separate concerns and stay that way:
"too much" is an argument error; "wrong status" comes from the state object.
THE RACE THIS CLOSES — over-refunding
A 100.00 transaction. Two threads each refund 60.00.
Both read remainingRefundable() == 100.00. Both pass the check.
Together they refund 120.00 of a 100.00 charge.
Classic check-then-act. The read and the write must be one step.
The lock is per TRANSACTION, not global — different txns never contend ✓
the charge path takes the SAME monitor, so a status flip never interleaves with a refund's read of it
IDEMPOTENCY — claim the key BEFORE you create anything
THE NAIVE ORDER — leaks a phantom row
if (idempotencyKeys.get(key) != null) return existing; // both miss
Transaction txn = new Transaction(...);
transactions.put(txnId, txn); // both publish!
idempotencyKeys.putIfAbsent(key, txnId); // one loses
The loser returns the winner's transaction — so there is no double
CHARGE. But it has already published an orphan transaction that is
reachable by id and will never be charged or reconciled.
In a real gateway that is a phantom row in the ledger.
THE FIX — invert the order
String txnId = "TXN-" + txnCounter.incrementAndGet();
if (idempotent) {
String owner = idempotencyKeys.putIfAbsent(key, txnId);
if (owner != null) return getTransaction(owner); // created NOTHING
} Transaction txn = new Transaction(txnId, ...); transactions.put(...);
putIfAbsent on a ConcurrentHashMap is an atomic CAS — exactly one
thread can win a given key.
The loser exits having allocated only a burnt counter value ✓
THE CAVEAT — state it before you're asked
The loser may observe the transaction while it is still PENDING, because
the winner charges AFTER publishing.
Real gateways return 409 Conflict + retry-after for an in-flight key, or
make the client poll. Blocking the loser on the winner's charge would be
worse — it couples an inbound request to an outbound network call.
WHY Money AND NOT double — the concrete failure
A 0.08 transaction, refunded in three parts: 0.06 + 0.01 + 0.01
Both consequences were reproduced against the real gateway before the fix:
1. the transaction NEVER reached REFUNDED — it sat in SUCCESS forever,
because remaining <= 0.0 was false
2. remaining was positive, so the gateway ACCEPTED A FOURTH REFUND on an
already fully-refunded transaction
Money — long minor units, and the invariant becomes representable
6 + 1 + 1 == 8, and remaining is exactly zero. Not "close to zero".
plus / minus use Math.addExact — an overflow throws instead of wrapping
silently to a negative balance. Mixing currencies throws instead of coercing.
the fix is not "round more carefully" — it is a TYPE where the invariant fits ✓
trade-off: long minor can't express sub-cent pricing; BigDecimal could, at the cost of scale management everywhere
ALL OF THIS, ONE LAYER DOWN
Idempotency → a UNIQUE index on idempotency_key;
insert-and-catch-duplicate is the same algorithm at DB level.
Refund bound → a conditional update:
UPDATE txn SET refunded = refunded + ? WHERE id = ? AND refunded + ? <= amount
… which needs no application lock at all ✓
SAY IT OUT LOUD:
"Three things must never happen: a double charge, a refund exceeding the capture, and a refund of a failed transaction. One CAS, one monitor, and one state object each."
"WHAT IF THE PROCESSOR CALL TIMES OUT?"
You don't know whether the charge landed. Persist PENDING before calling out (write-ahead), then reconcile: query the
processor by your own reference id, or let their webhook settle it.
Never retry a charge without an idempotency key on the OUTBOUND call too.
HONEST GAPS IN THIS IMPLEMENTATION
idempotencyKeys grows forever — a real memory leak; TTL it (24h is typical) or bound it with an LRU.
Key reuse with a DIFFERENT amount is not detected — store a request fingerprint and reject a mismatched reuse.
Processors are stubs (no network I/O), so partial failure is discussed but not coded. Transaction mutates instead of event-sourcing.

g.text: Patterns exercised here: State · Strategy · Flyweight · Factory · Value Object (Money) · CAS idempotency
